journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems

abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic design paradigm for physical design automation that fundamentally reconceptualizes placement optimization in VLSI systems. Unlike conventional cost-function-based approaches that rely on deterministic wirelength and congestion metrics, the proposed framework treats physical design as a stochastic optimization problem governed by information-theoretic principles. We develop a formal mathematical model that characterizes the relationship between module placement entropy and circuit performance variability, establishing theoretical bounds on achievable design quality under manufacturing uncertainties. The paradigm shift involves replacing gradient-descent-based algorithms with message-passing inference techniques borrowed from statistical physics, enabling simultaneous optimization of timing, power, and yield objectives. Rigorous proofs demonstrate that this approach attains globally optimal solutions with probability approaching one as problem scale increases, a property unattainable by existing deterministic methods. Extensive experiments on benchmark circuits up to 50 million instances validate that the proposed framework consistently discovers placement solutions that reduce total wirelength by 23-31% while improving timing slack by 18-25% compared to state-of-the-art physical design tools. This work establishes a new theoretical foundation for VLSI physical design that bridges the gap between combinatorial optimization theory and practical integrated circuit implementation, opening avenues for designing future complex system-on-chip architectures with predictable performance characteristics.

This paper presents a theoretically grounded improvement to Boolean satisfiability (SAT)-based resynthesis techniques for power optimization in low-power VLSI logic synthesis. Existing SAT-based approaches suffer from exponential runtime complexity that limits their practical applicability to large-scale integrated circuits. We develop a novel theoretical framework based on circuit controllability analysis that characterizes the relationship between input patterns and switching activity propagation. This framework enables significant pruning of the SAT solver's search space by identifying provably redundant reconvergence structures in circuit DAGs. The key theoretical contribution is a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for local don't-care computation that reduce the complexity of minimum-cost resubstitution from exponential to polynomial time for a large class of functions. We prove that the proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal power reductions while providing theoretical guarantees on solution quality. Experimental results on ISCAS and IWLS benchmark circuits demonstrate that the improved method achieves 15-22% additional power reduction over state-of-the-art power optimization tools while reducing runtime by 40-60%. The theoretical insights also enable scalable implementation for industrial-strength designs with millions of gates, addressing a critical limitation of previous SAT-based approaches in practical VLSI design flows.

This paper presents a fully integrated neuromorphic system-on-chip that implements a new computational paradigm for edge machine learning inference, fundamentally redefining the architecture of VLSI systems for artificial intelligence. The proposed chip introduces in-memory computing through non-volatile analog memory crossbars that perform matrix-vector multiplication directly within the memory array, eliminating the data movement bottleneck that制约 conventional von Neumann architectures. A novel event-driven mixed-signal processing pipeline processes sparse neural network activations with unprecedented energy efficiency. The chip integrates 16 million programmable synaptic elements fabricated in 28nm CMOS, supporting arbitrary neural network topologies through runtime reconfiguration. We introduce a paradigm shift from precision-based computation to stochastic spiking computation, where information is encoded in spike timing rather than binary values, enabling ultra-low-power operation for always-on AI applications. The complete system includes on-chip adaptive learning mechanisms that enable on-device continual learning without cloud connectivity. Measurement results demonstrate inference energy of 0.8 pJ per synaptic operation, representing a 100x improvement over state-of-the-art AI accelerators. This work establishes a new paradigm for VLSI systems that seamlessly integrates sensing, computation, and learning in a unified hardware-software co-design framework, enabling intelligent edge devices with cognitive capabilities previously achievable only in cloud data centers.

This paper presents a high-performance biomedical sensor interface SoC with significant improvements in power efficiency and signal integrity for implantable medical devices. The proposed system integrates a precision analog front-end, multi-channel data converter, and digital signal processor on a single chip, addressing critical challenges in neural recording and stimulation applications. We introduce an improved chopper-stabilized instrumentation amplifier topology that achieves 0.8 µV input-referred noise in a 0.01-500 Hz bandwidth while consuming only 1.2 µW per channel, representing a 40% power reduction compared to prior art. A novel multi-bit sigma-delta modulator architecture with gain-ranging feedback provides 90 dB dynamic range for neural signal acquisition with enhanced linearity. The digital back-end implements configurable spike detection and feature extraction algorithms optimized for ultra-low-power operation. A novel dual-mode power management unit enables seamless transitions between recording and stimulation modes, critical for closed-loop neuroprosthetic systems. The complete SoC, fabricated in 65nm CMOS, demonstrates 16-channel simultaneous neural recording with on-chip processing capability. Measurement results confirm that the improved design achieves 3x better energy efficiency per channel while maintaining superior signal quality for chronic implantable applications. This work provides a practical solution for next-generation neural interfaces requiring long-term battery-free operation powered by inductive coupling or energy harvesting.
